stimulus.body: Source note: Causes of the revolt of 1857. The 1857 revolt arose from military grievances, heavy land revenue, and political displacement, not from a single religious or economic cause.

questions.stem: Using the source note, explain causes of the 1857 revolt.

answer.exemplar: The 1857 revolt arose from military grievances, heavy land revenue, and political displacement, not from a single religious or economic cause.

questions.explanation: The revolt combined sepoy grievances, land revenue, and political change; reducing it to cartridges or economics alone misses the wider crisis.
questions.hint: Combine military, economic, and political causes.

questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: Describe the aims of Indian petitioning politics

stimulus.body: Indian associations petitioned Parliament for reform and representation. Their petitions sought rights within the empire rather than immediate separation. The method was legal and constitutional.

questions.stem: A source note on petitioning politics in India reads: "Sought reform, representation, and rights" Using that evidence, an Indian association petitioning Parliament; what did such petitions mainly seek?

options.text: Believes petitions demanded immediate independence
options.misconception: believes petitions demanded immediate independence

options.text: Thinks petitions were only about tax relief
options.misconception: thinks petitions were only about tax relief

options.text: Sought reform, representation, and rights
Views petitions as mere loyalty displays
options.misconception: views petitions as mere loyalty displays

questions.explanation: Petitions asked for reform and representation; they were not demands for immediate independence or mere displays of loyalty.
questions.hint: Petitions sought reform and rights, not revolt.

questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.topic: Boycott after the partition of Bengal
questions.learningObjective: Explain the aim of the Bengal boycott

stimulus.body: Source note: Sought to revive local industries and pride. This is the claim the evidence in the topic supports.

questions.stem: A source note on boycott after the partition of Bengal reads: "Sought to revive local industries and pride" Using that evidence, students refusing British cloth after 1905; what was the immediate aim of the swadeshi boycott?

options.text: Aimed only at punishing British merchants
options.misconception: aimed only at punishing British merchants

options.text: Demanded immediate partition reversal only
options.misconception: demanded immediate partition reversal only

options.text: Was mainly a religious conversion drive
options.misconception: was mainly a religious conversion drive

options.text: Sought to revive local industries and pride

questions.explanation: Swadeshi sought to revive local industry and pride; it was not only about merchants, partition reversal, or conversion.
questions.hint: Boycott aimed at local revival and pride.
